description.narrative: Det föreslagna stödet är till att HiH EA ska implementera ett program "Utveckling av inkluderande och motståndskraftiga företag" (DIRE) som består av två projekt förankrade i två möjlighetsområden: 1. MSME; 2. Waste to Resource (W2R – avfallshantering och cirkularitet). HiH EA föreslår att man ska använda sin fyrastegsmodell (med sju inbyggda modulära utbildningsmetoder) i utvecklingen av företag inom de två möjlighetsområdena. HiH EA strävar efter att arbeta med Bottom of the Pyramid (BoP) för att förmedla ekonomisk förvaltning/läskunnighet, inspirera företags inneboende uppfattning, förbättra ekonomisk tillgång samt stödja företag att knyta an till bredare marknader. Implementeringsstrategin och tillvägagångssättet har kompletterande kapacitetsbyggande tillvägagångssätt för att integrera företagsresiliens, skapa kapacitet för entreprenörer för byråkrati och mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhetsintegrering och spridning av planetvänliga metoder i företagsutveckling.

The proposed support is for HiH EA to implement a programme “Development of Inclusive and Resilient Enterprises” (DIRE) composed of two projects anchored on two opportunity areas of: 1. MSMEs; 2. Waste to Resource (W2R – waste management and circularity). HiH EA proposes to deploy its four step model (with seven in-built modular training approach) in development of enterprises in the two opportunity areas. HiH EA aims to work with the Bottom of the Pyramid (BoP) to impart financial management/literacy, inspire intrinsic conception of enterprises, enhance financial access as well as support enterprises to make linkage to broader markets. The implementation strategy and approach has complementary capacity building approach to integrate enterprise resilience, create capacity for agency in entrepreneurs for policy advocacy and human rights, gender mainstreaming, and deployment of planet friendly practices in enterprise development.

Goal Level: To contribute to the well being of the project direct participant through reduction of poverty and exclusion among willing people in both rural, urban, and peri- urban areas.
Purpose Level: To develop viable enterprises that will contribute to move direct project participants in rural, urban and peri-urban areas of 14 counties in Kenya from poverty to middle income status as envisaged in Kenyas Vision 2030.
Project key Outcomes
Outcome 1: Knowledge and skills on enterprise development among beneficiaries enhanced
Outcome 2: Appropriate market chains developed
Outcome 3: Resilience of enterprise development enhanced
Outcome 4: Organizational capacity for implementation and M&E is enhanced

Decision on Building Inclusive & Resilient Enterprises (BIRE) Contribution No (11408).

description.narrative:
As this was the inception phase, the focus was on laying the groundwork rather than delivering immediate outputs. Key deliverable under this phase included conducting the baseline survey, recruiting and onboarding the project team, carrying out the Market System Assessment (MSA) and designing interventions, developing selection criteria, and establishing implementation hubs that also serve as offices. Additionally, recruitment of Technical Assistance (TA) and submission of the revised ProDoc were completed.
A revised project document and work plan were submitted, now featuring well-defined selection criteria for both target actors and innovation grants. The revised ProDoc also clearly outlines team composition and roles, with the team capped at 22 direct staff and 7 indirect support staff, and an administration cost ceiling of 7%.
The responsibilities of Technical Assistance have been clearly outlined. This is a positive step, as it ensures alignment with the Market System Development (MSD) approach, strengthening the projects strategic direction.
As part of the foundational activities, 783 accelerator enterprises were engaged and 300 Bottom of the Pyramid Self-Help Groups were profiled. From these enterprises, the first cohort will be competitively selected using the agreed criteria and subsequently onboarded.
In preparation for capacity building, curricula and training guides were developed to support the training of 18 identified cooperatives.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
